title: An audit listing of a model's indicator constraints

blocks.text: A model reviewer at a water utility wants a plain listing of every indicator constraint in a model, to check them against the written rules without reading the code that built them. Write `audit(model)`, which returns one tuple per indicator constraint, in the order `model.get_indicator_constraints()` gives them:

items: `indicator_name`: the name of the indicator variable;
`active_value`: the value of the indicator at which the row must hold, `1` or `0`;
`lower`, `upper`: the row's bounds, with `-math.inf` or `math.inf` where a side has none;
`coefficients`: a dict from each variable name in the row to its coefficient.

blocks.text: So for $`z = 1 \Rightarrow 2a + 3b \le 10`$ named `cap`, the tuple is `("cap", "z", 1, -math.inf, 10.0, {"a": 2.0, "b": 3.0})`.
Read everything from the constraint objects: the tests build models you have not seen. Nothing needs solving. About eight lines.

from __future__ import annotations

import math

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


def audit(model: mathopt.Model) -> list[tuple]:
    """(name, indicator name, active value, lower, upper, {variable name: coefficient}) per indicator."""
    rows = []
    for ic in model.get_indicator_constraints():
        rows.append((ic.name, ic.indicator_variable.name, 0 if ic.activate_on_zero else 1,
                     ic.lower_bound, ic.upper_bound,
                     {term.variable.name: term.coefficient for term in ic.terms()}))
    return rows


if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = mathopt.Model()
    z, a, b = model.add_binary_variable(name="z"), model.add_variable(name="a"), model.add_variable(name="b")
    model.add_indicator_constraint(indicator=z, implied_constraint=2 * a + 3 * b <= 10, name="cap")
    print(audit(model), math.inf)

cases.says: a rule switched on at one with only an upper bound is listed with its name, indicator, active value, bounds and coefficients
a rule switched on at zero lists 0 as its active value, next to one switched on at one
a rule with a lower and an upper bound lists both
a rule whose variables have coefficients other than 1 lists those coefficients
